newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish exports fall 1 pct Jan-Nov '96.
newsitem.headline: Swedish exports fall 1 pct Jan-Nov '96.

text.p: Sweden's exports fell by one percent while imports fell by three percent between January and November 1996 compared to a year before, Statistics Sweden said on Friday.
Exports were worth 520.1 billion crowns ($70.2 billion) compared to 523 billion crowns a year earlier.
Stastistics Sweden said in a statement imports slipped to 409.3 billion crowns ($55.2 billion) from 422.3 billion crowns in the same period of 1995.
The figures were based on current prices.
Stastistics Sweden said the value of Sweden's trade with other European Union (EU) countries slipped last year.
Swedish exports to to the EU fell by six percent while imports fell by four percent.
Exports to the EU accounted for 57 percent of total Swedish exports.
Trade with Germany was weak with exports falling nine percent and imports down eight percent.
Germany is Sweden's most important trade patner and accounts for 12 percent of Swedish exports and 19 percent of imports.
